text:
maya: heads-up — we're seeing a bunch of 429 spikes on the eu-west cluster when batch jobs + interactive requests overlap. looks like the token-bucket per-key limits aren't matching GPU capacity and queues are growing.

omar: can you paste the tail of the logs? are these short-lived bursts or sustained? :thinking_face:

maya: short bursts ~1-2m, but when preemptible pools scale up slowly the backlog jumps. sample log: `2026-03-17T14:22:03Z WARN admission: queue_len=412 keys_blocked=23 gpu_util=95%`

li: hmm, sounds like classic mismatch: static per-key qps + large variance in seq lengths -> transient saturation. We probably need capacity-aware refill or admission control upstream.

anu: +1. What if we expose a dynamic token rate that's a function of available GPU slots? e.g. tokens_per_sec = base_rate * (free_slots / total_slots) with a floor. That would throttle orgs down gracefully when fleet is saturated.

omar: that avoids hard 429 storms. But need to be careful about fairness — bursty keys could monopolize free slots. Suggest hybrid: per-key token-bucket for short bursts, plus org-level circuit that reduces refill globally when node pressure crosses thresholds.

maya: sketch:
```
# pseudo
per_key_bucket: capacity=burst_k, refill=key_rate
org_bucket: capacity=org_burst, refill=org_rate_dynamic
admission: if org_bucket.tokens==0 -> queue request up to TTL else admit
backpressure_signal: when gpu_util>90% -> org_rate_dynamic *= 0.5
```

li: + add a small per-request admission check that rejects >16k token requests when fleet is at 95% (we already saw large seqs grind throughput). Also queue length should have a hard cap with immediate 503 fallback for non-critical routes.

omar: how do we calculate org_rate_dynamic reliably across regions? We need a capacity view: per-region free_gpus, pending_preemptible_provisions, and an estimate of tokens/sec per GPU for our model mix. That estimate is the tricky part.

maya: agree. propose a simple model first: assume median tokens/sec per GPU per model class from our perf profiles. compute available_capacity = sum(free_gpus_region * tokens_per_gpu_model). Then distribute a share to org proportional to their historical share or contractual reserved capacity.

anu: we also need hysteresis to avoid flapping when instances come up/down. e.g. only recompute dynamic refill every 30s and apply a smoothing factor alpha=0.2.

li: thoughts on queueing semantics? inline queue (nginx-level) vs external job-queue? inline is simple but can block worker threads. external queue lets us prioritize and surface metrics.

maya: prefer external lightweight queue (redis streams) with per-org priorities and TTL. admission will push metadata so workers can decide to preempt long requests if resources are tight.

omar: API-level headers to communicate limits: `X-RW-Rate-Limit: bucket=40,burst=80,reset=164` and `X-RW-Capacity-Estimate: region=eu-west,avail_tokens=12000`. Also emit `Retry-After` on 429s. Clients can choose to backoff.

anu: ops concerns — implementing dynamic refill will need a new service that watches cluster state and writes rates to the rate-limiter cache (redis). It must be sharded and tolerant to lag. If it dies, fallback to conservative static rates.

li: we should run an experiment on a canary org with synthetic traffic (mixed short/chat + long-infer) and simulate scale-down events. measure 95p latency, 429 rate, and wasted tokens due to preemption.

maya: action items:
- maya: prototype dynamic-refill service (watcher + simple capacity estimator) — due EOW
- omar: add org-level token-bucket + queue TTL support to rate-limiter — Weds
- li: design canary traffic harness + metrics (95/99 latency, 429/503) — Thurs
- anu: write rollout plan + safety knobs (floor rates, hysteresis, fallback) — Thurs

omar: thanks. one more: add a metrics tag to all admission events: `admission.reason={burst,capacity,overlong}` so we can do root-cause.

maya: noted. i'll post a short design doc once prototype is up. :rocket:

infra-bot: deploy-checklist: ensure redis cluster has >10% headroom, add new metrics endpoint `/v1/rl/health`, and create canary org id `canary-dynamic-rl`.

li: perfect. keeping expectations low for EOW but this feels actionable.

maya: cool — thanks everyone. will ping when demo ready. :thumbsup:
